scope: Universal necessary positive closed intermediate-current and dd^c-closed complementary-test restrictions. Complete classification of all honest smooth fixed-mass shrinking defects on the scalar Hopf threefold for every Hermitian metric: arbitrary positive base measures lifted with normalized metric-area fiber conditionals, exact supports, no point atoms, pluripolarity equivalence and all charging fractions. exact_task.problem:
Let (X,omega) be a connected compact complex Hermitian manifold of dimension n with infinite upper bounded-potential Monge-Ampere mass v_+(omega). Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial and genuine omega-psh functions: locally they are a genuine plurisubharmonic function plus a smooth function, with the canonical upper representative and omega+dd^c u>=0. Write V_omega=integral_X omega^n, fix b>V_omega and epsilon_j->0. The shrinking construction chooses smooth u_j with sup_X u_j=0, omega+dd^c u_j>=0, and 0<s_j<epsilon_j such that w_j=s_j u_j has integral_X(omega+dd^c w_j)^n=b. Thus omega+dd^c w_j>=(1-epsilon_j)omega and w_j->0 in capacity. After passage to a subsequence, (omega+dd^c w_j)^n converges weakly to omega^n+sigma, where sigma>=0 has mass b-V_omega. Every fixed shallow restriction 1_{w_j>=-T}(omega+dd^c w_j)^n converges in total variation to omega^n, and every fixed deep restriction 1_{w_j<-T}(omega+dd^c w_j)^n converges weakly to sigma. The coefficient currents converge in L1 and their smooth Gauduchon traces in total variation. These linear facts do not imply convergence of nonlinear products. The construction allows arbitrary large-mass smooth u_j; it is not restricted to a specific radial Hopf profile.

Original S01 asks which supports and pluripolar charging behaviors are possible for these defect measures: establish necessary support restrictions, decide whether they must or may charge pluripolar sets, and determine what prescribed measures can actually be realized by honest shrinking sequences. The standard Hopf threefold provides a concrete infinite-upper-mass setting: X=(C^3 minus {0})/<z->exp(-1)z>, s=log|z|^2, alpha=dd^c s, beta=ds wedge d^c s, omega=alpha+beta. Here alpha is pulled back from Fubini-Study on P2, ddc omega=-alpha^2, dd^c omega^2=0 and integral omega^3=6; its smooth mass is 6+6 integral_P2 integral_fiber |u_w|^2 dA_E omega_FS^2 in the local fiber coordinate w=log z0, with the fiber Haar area normalized to one. This mass identity and existence of large-mass potentials are background, not a proof identifying sigma. Distinguish restrictions forced by the general shrinking construction from results only for a named explicit family or manifold. No candidate support, limit formula, realization construction or proof is supplied.

notes.summary: On the standard Hopf threefold, an honest shrinking potential f with curvature ≥−tω and fixed excess mass m has a positive quadratic defect carrier ν=3ω∧(dd^c f+tω)^2. Its mass is m+3t²V, and MA(f)−ω³−ν tends to zero in total variation as t→0. This special nonlinear reduction follows from Stokes and dd^cω²=0; it is not a general Hermitian assertion.
notes.detailedSummary: Let V=∫ω³ and M(f)=∫(ω+dd^c f)³ on the Hopf threefold. For every smooth real f, M(f)=V+3Q(f), where Q(f)=∫ω∧(dd^c f)²=∫df∧d^c f∧α², and M(λf)−V=λ²(M(f)−V). If dd^c f≥−tω, H=dd^c f+tω is positive and, writing m=M(f)−V, its three relevant masses are ∫ω²H=tV, ∫ωH²=m/3+t²V, and ∫H³=tm+t³V. For 0<t<1 and m≥0, the exact positive expansion gives ||MA(f)−ω³−3ωH²||TV≤6tV+2tm+4t³V. Thus bounded-mass honest shrinking sequences have their complete defect limits identified by the quadratic positive measures, not merely by their total masses. The proof uses only supplied Hopf differential identities and Stokes. It does not identify the quadratic limit of any particular initial sequence.
notes.text:
Work on the standard Hopf threefold in the problem. Write D=dd^c, V=∫_X ω³ (=6 under the stated normalization), and M(f)=∫_X(ω+Df)³ for a smooth real function f. The supplied differential identities are Dω²=0 and Dω=−α². All wedge products below are of smooth forms, so Stokes applies without a singular-product issue.

1. Quadratic mass identity reconstructed by Stokes.

First, ∫ω²∧Df=∫f Dω²=0. Also ∫(Df)³=0, since (Df)³=D(f(Df)²). Consequently

  M(f)=V+3Q(f),    Q(f):=∫ω∧(Df)².

Since D(f Df)=(Df)²,

  Q(f)=∫f Df∧Dω.

With d^c=(i/(4π))(bar∂−∂), one has D(f²/2)=df∧d^c f+f Df. The D(f²/2) term integrates to zero against the d-closed form Dω. It follows that

  Q(f)=−∫df∧d^c f∧Dω=∫df∧d^c f∧α²≥0.

This also proves exactly, rather than asymptotically,

  M(λf)−V=λ²(M(f)−V)

for every real λ. These identities hold for every smooth f, not just a special radial profile. No fiberwise formula is needed here.

2. A positive carrier for the nonlinear defect.

Suppose 0<t<1 and Df≥−tω. Set H=Df+tω≥0, and put m=M(f)−V=3Q(f). Expanding and using the identities above gives

  ∫ω²∧H=tV,
  ∫ω∧H²=m/3+t²V,
  ∫H³=tm+t³V.

In particular all three are masses of positive forms. The final formula is sometimes especially useful: the pure cubic positive term has mass tending to zero when t→0 and m stays bounded, despite the nonzero Monge–Ampère defect.

Define the positive top-degree measure ν(f,t)=3ω∧H². Its mass is m+3t²V. The exact expansion is

  (ω+Df)³=(1−t)³ω³+3(1−t)²ω²∧H+(1−t)ν(f,t)+H³.

Every term displayed on the right is positive. Subtracting ω³+ν(f,t) and using their masses therefore yields the quantitative signed-measure estimate

  ||(ω+Df)³−ω³−ν(f,t)||TV
  ≤[1−(1−t)³]V+3(1−t)²tV+t(m+3t²V)+(tm+t³V)
  ≤6tV+2tm+4t³V.

Thus, if t_j→0, Df_j≥−t_jω, and m_j=M(f_j)−V is bounded and nonnegative, then

  (ω+Df_j)³−ω³−3ω∧(Df_j+t_jω)² →0 in total variation.

In particular, for an original fixed-mass sequence f_j=s_j u_j with excess mass m=b−V, weak convergence of its Monge–Ampère measures to ω³+σ is equivalent to weak convergence of the positive quadratic carriers 3ω∧(Df_j+s_jω)² to σ. This is a full local weak-measure identification, not just an integrated mass equality.

3. Scope and remaining gap.

The reduction uses special threefold identities. It does not follow from linear current convergence and it is not asserted on arbitrary Hermitian manifolds or in arbitrary dimension. It does not by itself tell us the supports or pluripolar charging of a carrier limit. Subsequent notes use it to build actual sequences whose carrier limits are prescribed. The only geometric premises used here are the differential identities supplied in the problem; the nonlinear calculation itself has been reconstructed.

reconstruction.proof:
Write D=dd^c. Integration by parts on the compact manifold gives ∫ω²∧Df=∫fDω²=0. Since Df is d-closed, (Df)³=d(d^cf∧(Df)²), and its integral is zero. Also (Df)²=D(fDf), so Q(f)=∫fDf∧Dω. Using D(f²/2)=fDf+df∧d^cf and D(Dω)=0 gives
Q(f)=−∫df∧d^cf∧Dω=∫df∧d^cf∧α²≥0.
Indeed df∧d^cf=(i/(2π))∂f∧bar∂f and α² are semipositive. The cube expansion now proves M(f)=V+3Q(f). Since Q(λf)=λ²Q(f), it also proves the scaling identity for every real λ.

For H=Df+tω≥0, direct expansion gives
∫ω²H=tV,
∫ωH²=Q(f)+t²V=m/3+t²V,
∫H³=3tQ(f)+t³V=tm+t³V.
These wedge products are positive. Since ω+Df=(1−t)ω+H, the asserted measure decomposition is the binomial identity. After subtracting ω³+ν, the remaining four terms are ((1−t)³−1)ω³, 3(1−t)²ω²H, −tν, and H³. Their total variation norms are bounded by their respective positive masses, giving the first displayed bound. Its first two terms are at most 3tV each; the last two sum to 2tm+4t³V. This gives the second bound.

For bounded m_j and t_j→0 the bound tends to zero. For an honest sequence take t_j=s_j, so H_j=s_j(ω+Du_j)≥0 and m_j=b−V. Consequently the difference between its Monge–Ampère measure and ω³+3ωH_j² tends to zero in total variation. This proves the weak-limit equivalence and all assertions of the note for the stated metric.

notes.summary: Constructs honest smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequences on the standard Hopf threefold with the prescribed diffuse defect σ=((b−V)/V)ω³. Therefore defects can have full support and charge no pluripolar sets. The construction averages many randomly translated large-mass potentials at the potential level, controls positive mixed quadratic terms, chooses deterministic samples, and makes an exact final mass rescaling. It does not classify all defects or decide whether pluripolar-charging examples exist.
notes.detailedSummary: For the Hopf metric, the compact transitive group G=U(3)×(R/Z) preserves ω. Given any large-mass smooth normalized ω-psh u, put f=su with M(f)=b and s arbitrarily small; the exact choice is s=√((b−V)/(M(u)−V)). Take N independent invariantly distributed translates and W=N^(−1/2)∑g_l^*f. Then H_W=DW+s√N ω=N^(−1/2)∑g_l^*(Df+sω)≥0. The diagonal part of 3ωH_W² is an empirical average of bounded-mass positive measures; its expected measure is ((b−V)+3s²V)ω³/V. Its positive off-diagonal part has expected mass 3(N−1)s²V. With N→∞ and s√N→0 sufficiently fast, elementary variance and Markov bounds select deterministic translates making the diagonal converge to ((b−V)/V)ω³ and the off-diagonal vanish in total variation. The quadratic mass identity then gives M(W)→b. Rescale by λ=√((b−V)/(M(W)−V))→1 and normalize the averaged underlying potential to supremum zero. The resulting smooth normalized ω-psh U has shrinking parameter s'=λs√N<ε_j, exact mass b, and the carrier calculation proves the complete weak limit (ω+dd^c(s'U))³→(b/V)ω³. Capacity convergence and the other stated shrinking properties follow because this is precisely an honest sequence of the type stipulated in the problem. Since smooth volume vanishes on pluripolar sets, these defects have full support but no pluripolar charge.
notes.text:
THEOREM (a prescribed diffuse defect on the standard Hopf threefold). Let X and ω be the standard Hopf threefold and metric in the problem. Assume the supplied existence of smooth normalized ω-psh potentials of arbitrarily large mass. For every b>V=∫ω³ and every positive ε_j→0, there are smooth U_j with sup_X U_j=0 and ω+dd^c U_j≥0, and parameters 0<r_j<ε_j, such that

  ∫(ω+dd^c(r_j U_j))³=b,
  (ω+dd^c(r_j U_j))³ → (b/V)ω³ weakly.

They are honest shrinking sequences, hence retain the capacity and fixed-level properties stated in the question. Their defect is the prescribed measure σ=((b−V)/V)ω³. In particular its support is all of X and it charges no pluripolar sets.

This theorem supplies realizable examples, not a classification of arbitrary shrinking sequences. It uses arbitrary large-mass smooth potentials, not a presumed special Hopf profile.

PROOF.

A. An explicit invariant averaging distribution.

The compact group G=U(3)×(R/Z) acts on X by

  (A,t)[z]=[e^t A z].

Changing t by an integer changes only the deck representative. The action is holomorphic and transitive: one can first match norms by real scaling and then match unit vectors by a unitary matrix. It preserves ω, because unitary maps leave s=log|z|² unchanged and real scaling adds a constant to s, leaving α=dd^c s and β=ds∧d^c s unchanged.

One may use the usual invariant probability h on this group. To avoid an unverified group-measure premise, it can be constructed as follows. Take a 3×3 complex Gaussian matrix Z with density proportional to exp(−Tr(Z*Z)) and let A=Z(Z*Z)^(−1/2), defined almost surely. Left and right unitary invariance of the Gaussian law, and equivariance of this polar expression, make the law of A left and right invariant. Independently take t uniform modulo 1. This supplies the required left and right invariant probability on G.

For every smooth q, the function ∫q∘g dh(g) is constant, by transitivity and right invariance. Therefore averaging commutes with dd^c and

  ∫g^*(dd^c q+sω) dh(g)=sω.

For every finite positive measure η, averaging its translates gives

  ∫g^*η dh(g)=(η(X)/V)ω³.

For completeness, on testing against a continuous φ, the inner average of φ∘g^(−1) is independent of the point by transitivity; integrating it against the invariant probability ω³/V identifies its constant as V^(−1)∫φω³. This proves the displayed top-degree averaging identity directly.

B. Start with one arbitrarily small fixed-mass shrink.

Put m=b−V>0. For any desired upper bound on s, select a smooth normalized ω-psh u with sufficiently large M(u). By note n1,

  s=√(m/(M(u)−V)),   f=su

gives M(f)=V+m=b, and s can be as small as desired. Let

  H=dd^c f+sω≥0,    ν=3ω∧H².

Note n1 gives ν(X)=m+3s²V and ∫ω²H=sV.

Take N independent group elements g_1,...,g_N with distribution h. Define

  W=N^(−1/2)∑_{l=1}^N f∘g_l,
  τ=s√N,
  K=dd^c W+τω=N^(−1/2)∑_{l=1}^N g_l^*H≥0.

The quadratic carrier of W decomposes into two positive measures:

  3ω∧K²=D_N+C_N,
  D_N=(1/N)∑_{l=1}^N g_l^*ν,
  C_N=(6/N)∑_{l<k}ω∧g_l^*H∧g_k^*H.

This is an averaging of actual potentials, not a formal averaging of their Monge–Ampère measures.

C. The mixed terms really vanish, and the empirical measures can be chosen deterministically.

Independence, Fubini, and the form-average identity give

  E[C_N(X)]=3(N−1)s²V.

Indeed each independent mixed integral has expectation ∫ω∧(sω)²=s²V. Positivity permits a Markov estimate on the entire off-diagonal measure.

The variables Y_l(φ)=∫φ g_l^*ν have absolute value at most (m+3s²V)||φ||∞. For ||φ||∞≤1 their empirical average has variance at most (m+3s²V)²/N, and its mean is

  ((m+3s²V)/V)∫φω³.

Here variance follows directly by independence; no limit theorem is needed.

Choose a countable uniformly dense collection of real continuous test functions φ_k in the unit ball of C(X). Choose δ_j↓0, with δ_j<m/10. At step j choose N_j→∞ large enough that, for s≤1,

  j(m+3V)²/(N_j δ_j²)<1/4.

Then choose the large-mass potential and its s_j so small that

  τ_j=s_j√N_j<min(ε_j/4,1/j,1/4),
  3Vτ_j²<m/2,
  3(N_j−1)s_j²V<δ_j/4.

The probability that any of the first j empirical test errors exceeds δ_j is less than 1/4 by the variance bound and a union bound. The probability that C_N(X)>δ_j is less than 1/4 by Markov. Hence there is a deterministic tuple of smooth translates for which both conclusions hold. Fix such a tuple at each j.

Its diagonal measures satisfy

  D_j → (m/V)ω³ weakly,

and its off-diagonal measures satisfy ||C_j||TV=C_j(X)≤δ_j→0. Thus

  3ω∧K_j² → (m/V)ω³ weakly.

This proves the desired complete local quadratic measure limit, using all continuous tests rather than only the mass.

D. Exact fixed mass, not just an asymptotically fixed mass.

Since K_j=dd^c W_j+τ_jω, the identities in n1 give

  M(W_j)−V=3∫ωK_j²−3τ_j²V
            =m+C_j(X)−3(N_j−1)s_j²V=:d_j.

Thus d_j→m. Our parameter choice ensures d_j≥m−3Vτ_j²>m/2 at every step. Define

  λ_j=√(m/d_j).

Then λ_j→1, λ_j≤√2, and M(λ_jW_j)=V+m=b exactly.

Let a_j=(1/N_j)∑u_j∘g_l and c_j=sup_X a_j. Set

  U_j=a_j−c_j,
  r_j=λ_jτ_j,
  w_j=r_jU_j.

The averaged a_j, and hence U_j, is a smooth genuine ω-psh function; sup U_j=0. Also 0<r_j<ε_j. The function w_j differs from λ_jW_j only by a constant. Consequently its mass is exactly b and

  ω+dd^c w_j≥(1−r_j)ω≥(1−ε_j)ω.

Its positive carrier is

  dd^c w_j+r_jω=λ_jK_j,
  3ω∧(dd^c w_j+r_jω)²=λ_j²(D_j+C_j) → (m/V)ω³.

Applying the total-variation reduction of n1 with t=r_j and fixed excess mass m now proves

  (ω+dd^c w_j)³ → ω³+(m/V)ω³=(b/V)ω³

against every continuous test function. This is the complete local weak Monge–Ampère limit.

E. Retained shrinking properties and support/pluripolarity.

The final sequence has exactly the form stipulated in the problem: smooth normalized genuine ω-psh U_j, parameters r_j<ε_j, and exact fixed mass b. Thus the shrinking capacity conclusion supplied in the problem applies directly: w_j→0 in capacity. Likewise its supplied fixed shallow/deep and coefficient-current conclusions apply. No differently normalized potential class or nonlinear averaging assertion has been substituted.

The defect σ=(m/V)ω³ is a positive smooth volume measure, with support X because ω is Hermitian. A pluripolar set has Lebesgue measure zero: locally it is contained in the −∞ locus of a non-identically−∞ psh function, and such a psh function is locally integrable. Smooth volume therefore vanishes on every pluripolar set.

Accordingly defects need not have proper support and need not charge pluripolar sets. In particular a universal requirement that defects be supported on a pluripolar set, or that every defect have a nonzero pluripolar part, is false. Nothing in this proof shows that every defect is diffuse, and the possibility of pluripolar-charging defects remains unresolved.

Premise accounting: existence of arbitrarily large-mass smooth potentials and the shrinking capacity statement are used as background explicitly supplied by the task. The nonlinear reduction, averaging distribution, positive mixed-term estimates, deterministic selection, exact mass adjustment, and full weak limit are proved above. No source-dependent assertion about the defect of a particular initial Hopf profile is used.

correctness.report: Conditional on declared support n1, the realization proof is established. The group action is transitive and preserves ω, and the Gaussian polar construction supplies the required invariant distribution. Independence gives the mixed-term expected mass 3(N−1)s²V; the empirical variance bound is uniform despite the changing initial potential. Choosing N before the arbitrarily small s permits deterministic samples satisfying all finitely many test estimates while the positive mixed measure vanishes in total variation. Bounded masses and dense continuous tests then establish the complete weak carrier limit. The exact excess d_j=m+C_j(X)−3(N_j−1)s_j²V stays above m/2, so the final rescaling is legitimate, tends to one, and enforces mass b exactly. The normalized averaged potential is smooth genuine ω-psh, with shrinking parameter below ε_j. Thus n1 applies, and the task-granted capacity and fixed-level properties retain their exact scope. The pluripolar conclusion uses the local-integrability fact listed below; its standard submean argument bounds the negative integral near finite points and propagates through overlapping neighborhoods. Both summaries correctly describe this single prescribed diffuse realization and leave pluripolar-charging realizations and full classification unresolved.

and

The coefficients of dd^c w_j converge to zero in L¹, and for every fixed smooth Gauduchon metric γ with dd^cγ²=0, the trace measures γ²∧(ω+dd^c w_j) converge to γ²∧ω in total variation.

Thus the prescribed defect σ=((b−V)/V)ω³ is realizable by an honest smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequence with any prescribed shrinking bounds. Its support is X, and it gives zero mass to every pluripolar set. In particular, defects need not have proper support, need not be supported on pluripolar sets, and need not have any nonzero pluripolar charge. This is an existence theorem on this Hopf threefold, not a classification of its arbitrary shrinking sequences or a claim that all defects avoid pluripolar sets.
reconstruction.proof:
Put m=b−V>0. First construct a source sequence. Choose smooth normalized ω-psh u_k with M(u_k)−V arbitrarily large and set s_k=sqrt(m/(M(u_k)−V)), choosing the masses so that 0<s_k<1/k. By n1, f_k=s_ku_k has exact mass V+m. Write H_k=Df_k+s_kω≥0 and ν_k=3ωH_k². Then ∫ω²H_k=s_kV and ν_k(X)=m+3s_k²V. After extraction the fixed-mass Monge–Ampère measures converge weakly. Their lower bounds (1−s_k)³ω³ show that the limit is ω³+σ, with σ≥0 and σ(X)=m. By n1, ν_k→σ.

The compact group G=U(3)×(R/Z), acting by [z]↦[e^tAz], is holomorphic, transitive and preserves ω: s changes only by the constant 2t, while U(3) preserves |z|. Matching radii modulo e^Z and then unit vectors proves transitivity. Its normalized bi-invariant volume is a Haar probability h. For every continuous φ, ∫Gφ(g⁻¹x)dh(g) is independent of x; integrating against the invariant probability ω³/V identifies that constant. Therefore ∫Gg*σ dh(g)=(m/V)ω³, with g* meaning pushforward by g⁻¹. Finite partitions of the compact group of diameter tending to zero approximate h by finitely supported probabilities. Since g↦∫φ d(g*σ) is continuous, their finite orbital mixtures τ_j tend weakly to (m/V)ω³.

Here is a construction with actual potentials realizing those mixtures. For fixed finitely many g_a and weights θ_a summing to one, omit zero weights and put c_a=sqrt(θ_a). Successively choose source indices k_a and define
F=Σ_a c_a(f_{k_a}∘g_a), t=Σ_a c_as_{k_a}, H_F=DF+tω=Σ_a c_ag_a*H_{k_a}≥0.
The diagonal terms of 3ωH_F² are θ_ag_a*ν_{k_a}. The other terms are positive mixed measures. After a previous index a is chosen, its smooth form satisfies g_a*H_{k_a}≤C_aω. For a later index b,
∫ω g_a*H_{k_a}g_b*H_{k_b}≤C_a∫ω²g_b*H_{k_b}=C_as_{k_b}V.
Thus successive sufficiently large choices make all mixed masses arbitrarily small, while approximating each desired diagonal measure on any finite continuous test list. Simultaneously t can be made arbitrarily small. This proves weak and total-mass approximation by 3ωH_F² without averaging nonlinear Monge–Ampère measures.

At stage j apply this construction to τ_j, with errors tending to zero on the first j tests of a countable uniformly dense family in C(X), including the constant test. Require t_j<min(ε_j/4,1/j). The errors can additionally ensure
m_j:=M(F_j)−V=∫3ωH_{F_j}²−3t_j²V→m,
with m_j>0 and λ_j=sqrt(m/m_j)<2. Set
w_j=λ_j(F_j−sup_XF_j), r_j=λ_jt_j, U_j=(F_j−sup_XF_j)/t_j.
These are smooth actual functions, sup U_j=0, DU_j≥−ω, and w_j=r_jU_j with 0<r_j<ε_j. Constants do not affect derivatives or mass; n1 gives M(w_j)=V+λ_j²m_j=b. The positive carriers are H_{w_j}=λ_jH_{F_j}. Thus 3ωH_{w_j}²→(m/V)ω³. Bounded masses extend convergence from the dense test family to every continuous test. The total variation estimate of n1 proves (ω+Dw_j)³→(b/V)ω³. Also ω+Dw_j=(1−r_j)ω+H_{w_j}≥(1−r_j)ω≥(1−ε_j)ω.

All constructed functions satisfy the honest normalized shrinking hypotheses. Therefore the capacity and fixed shallow/deep conclusions granted in the task apply. For completeness the linear conclusions also follow directly: ∫ω²H_{w_j}=r_jV, so positivity bounds its coefficient L¹ norms by O(r_j), and those of Dw_j tend to zero. For a given Gauduchon γ, integration by parts gives ∫γ²H_{w_j}=r_j∫γ²ω, whence the total variation norm of γ²Dw_j is at most 2r_j∫γ²ω.

The realized defect is a positive multiple of the smooth strictly positive volume ω³ and has support X. The exact psh L¹ premise permitted in this note makes local −∞ loci Lebesgue-null. A countable coordinate cover then gives zero outer smooth-volume measure to every locally pluripolar set. Thus this defect has no pluripolar charge. This is an existence theorem, not a restriction on every defect.

notes.summary: General necessary structure: for every honest fixed-mass shrinking sequence, the defect is a sum Σ_{k=2}^{n−1} binom(n,k) ω^{n−k}∧K_k, where K_k are positive d-closed currents annihilating all smooth d-closed complementary forms. Consequently σ is supported in the degeneracy locus of every global smooth d-closed semipositive (1,1)-form. Pure top-power concentration vanishes. This is a genuine general restriction, not a Hopf-only result.
notes.detailedSummary: Set H_j=dd^c w_j+s_jω=s_j(ω+dd^c u_j)≥0. The positive expansion of MA(w_j)=((1−s_j)ω+H_j)^n with total mass b uniformly bounds every ∫ω^{n−k}H_j^k. The supplied Gauduchon trace property, or its immediate Stokes formula, gives H_j→0 with mass O(s_j). Since d(H_j^k)=ks_j dω∧H_j^{k−1}, all current limits K_k are d-closed. For every smooth d-closed real complementary form η, exactness of (dd^c w_j)^k=(H_j−s_jω)^k gives ∫ηH_j^k=O(s_j), using the lower-power mass bounds. Thus every K_k has zero pairings with all such η. Taking k=n and η=1 also proves H_j^n(X)=O(s_j), so K_n=0. Expanding the full measures then identifies σ with the stated sum, with K_1=K_n=0. If θ is any global smooth closed semipositive (1,1)-form, ∫θ^{n−k}K_k=0; positivity forces all K_k to vanish where θ is positive definite. Hence supp σ⊂{θ^n=0}, for every such θ. No assertion that these necessary current conditions suffice for realization is made.
notes.text:
GENERAL NECESSARY CURRENT AND SUPPORT RESTRICTIONS.

Let (X,ω) and an honest shrinking sequence be exactly as in the problem, in arbitrary complex dimension n. Write D=dd^c, w_j=s_j u_j, and

  H_j=Dw_j+s_jω=s_j(ω+Du_j)≥0.

Thus ω+Dw_j=(1−s_j)ω+H_j. We work after discarding finitely many indices so that s_j<1/2. Suppose the measures have weak limit ω^n+σ and total mass b, as stipulated.

1. Uniform bounds on every positive power.

The pointwise positive expansion

  (ω+Dw_j)^n=Σ_{k=0}^n binom(n,k)(1−s_j)^{n−k} ω^{n−k}∧H_j^k

and total mass b imply, for every k,

  ∫ω^{n−k}∧H_j^k ≤ 2^{n−k}b/binom(n,k).

These bounds control all coefficients of the positive currents H_j^k in finite coordinate charts: relative to a fixed positive metric, the diagonal coefficients are bounded by the trace, and positivity bounds off-diagonal coefficients by the diagonal ones. Thus a common subsequence has weak current limits K_k≥0 for all k. This compactness is simply compactness of bounded coefficient measures, applied in finitely many charts and then diagonally.

The first power actually tends to zero. One can use the linear/Gauduchon trace property supplied in the problem. More explicitly, for a smooth Gauduchon metric γ used for that trace, Dγ^{n−1}=0 and Stokes gives

  ∫γ^{n−1}∧H_j=s_j∫γ^{n−1}∧ω.

Metric comparison controls the ω-trace by this trace. Therefore H_j has current mass O(s_j), and K_1=0. This uses the available smooth Gauduchon trace, not convergence of any nonlinear product.

2. All limiting powers are d-closed.

Since dH_j=s_j dω,

  d(H_j^k)=k s_j dω∧H_j^{k−1}.

Testing against a fixed smooth form, the right side is bounded by a constant times s_j∫ω^{n−k+1}H_j^{k−1}. The preceding positive mass bounds show it tends to zero. Consequently dK_k=0.

3. Their closed-form pairings vanish; the top power vanishes altogether.

Let η be any smooth real d-closed form of degree 2n−2k. Exactness of Dw_j gives

  ∫η∧(Dw_j)^k=0.

Indeed (Dw_j)^k=d(d^c w_j∧(Dw_j)^{k−1}), and η is closed. Substitute Dw_j=H_j−s_jω and expand:

  ∫η∧H_j^k
  =−Σ_{r=0}^{k−1} binom(k,r)(−s_j)^{k−r}
       ∫η∧ω^{k−r}∧H_j^r.

The absolute value of each integral in this sum is bounded by a constant depending on η and ω times ∫ω^{n−r}H_j^r. Hence ∫ηH_j^k=O(s_j). Passing to the limit,

  ∫η∧K_k=0

for every smooth d-closed complementary real form η. These are precise zero de Rham pairings; no cohomological representation theorem is needed for the assertion. In the usual current-cohomology terminology the K_k are cohomologically trivial closed currents.

For k=n take η=1. The same computation gives ∫H_j^n=O(s_j). Since H_j^n is a positive measure, it tends to zero in total variation. Therefore K_n=0. This rules out a pure top-power defect even though intermediate products can be nonzero.

4. Identification of the general defect.

Pass to the common subsequence in the positive expansion. The k=0 term tends to ω^n, the first and last powers vanish, and multiplication by fixed smooth forms is continuous on currents. Hence

  σ=Σ_{k=2}^{n−1} binom(n,k) ω^{n−k}∧K_k.

Every summand is positive. The total mass of this sum is b−V_ω. For n=3 this simplifies to

  σ=3ω∧K_2,

where K_2 is positive, d-closed, and has all zero closed-form pairings. For n≤2 the sum is empty, so a positive fixed excess mass cannot occur in an honest shrinking construction of the stipulated type.

5. A concrete general support restriction.

Let θ be any GLOBAL smooth d-closed semipositive real (1,1)-form on X. For every k in the defect sum, η=θ^{n−k} is a smooth closed complementary form, so

  ∫θ^{n−k}∧K_k=0.

The integrand is a positive measure and therefore vanishes identically. Where θ is positive definite, its relevant power dominates a positive constant times ω^{n−k} on every relatively compact subregion. Thus K_k vanishes on that open set. It follows that

  supp σ ⊂ {x∈X : θ_x is not positive definite}={θ^n=0}.

This holds simultaneously for every global smooth closed semipositive θ. In particular a globally positive closed θ forces σ=0. The global hypothesis is essential: the argument does not apply merely because a coordinate neighborhood carries a local Kähler form.

These are necessary restrictions forced by the general shrinking construction, not merely by a named profile. They do not assert that every positive closed zero-pairing current, or every measure supported in the indicated degeneracy sets, can be realized. No external nonlinear-continuity theorem has been used: all products before taking limits are smooth, and the limits are controlled by positivity, Stokes, and the supplied linear trace property.

Testing the exact form (Dw_j)^k against a closed complementary form and expanding H_j−s_jω proves the zero pairings. For k=n this also proves total-variation disappearance of the positive top power. Passing to a common subsequence therefore gives exactly the stated defect decomposition. For a global closed semipositive θ, the zero pairing with θ^{n−k}, positivity, and metric domination on its positive-definite locus establish the support restriction. Both summaries preserve the global hypothesis and necessary-only character; the n≤2 obstruction is correctly conditional on such a shrinking construction. No additional nonroutine external premise is needed.

Let (X,ω) be a connected compact complex Hermitian manifold of complex dimension n with v_+(ω)=∞, let D=dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄, and put V_ω=∫_Xωⁿ. Fix b>V_ω and positive ε_j→0. Let u_j be smooth genuine ω-psh functions with sup_Xu_j=0, let 0<s_j<ε_j, and set w_j=s_j u_j. Assume ∫_X(ω+Dw_j)ⁿ=b and, along the sequence under consideration, (ω+Dw_j)ⁿ→ωⁿ+σ weakly, with σ≥0 of mass b−V_ω. Set H_j=Dw_j+s_jω=s_j(ω+Du_j)≥0.

For every 0≤k≤n and all sufficiently large j with s_j<1/2,
∫_Xω^{n−k}∧H_j^k≤2^{n−k}b/binom(n,k).
There is a common subsequence on which H_j^k converge as currents to positive currents K_k of bidegree (k,k), for 1≤k≤n. The first powers satisfy ∫_Xω^{n−1}∧H_j=O(s_j), so K_1=0. For every smooth Gauduchon metric γ with Dγ^{n−1}=0,
∫_Xγ^{n−1}∧H_j=s_j∫_Xγ^{n−1}∧ω.
Every K_k is d-closed. For every k and every smooth real d-closed form η of degree 2n−2k,
∫_Xη∧K_k=0.
The top powers satisfy ∫_XH_jⁿ=O(s_j), hence H_jⁿ→0 in total variation and K_n=0.

On the common subsequence the defect has the representation
σ=Σ_{k=2}^{n−1}binom(n,k)ω^{n−k}∧K_k,
with positive summands of total mass b−V_ω. In dimension three this is σ=3ω∧K_2. In dimensions n≤2, an honest shrinking sequence with a positive fixed excess mass b−V_ω cannot exist.

For every global smooth real d-closed semipositive (1,1)-form θ and every 2≤k≤n−1, the positive measure θ^{n−k}∧K_k vanishes identically. Each K_k, and hence σ, vanishes on the open set where θ is positive definite. Thus, simultaneously for every such θ,
supp σ⊂{x∈X:θ_x is not positive definite}={θⁿ=0}.
A global positive d-closed (1,1)-form forces σ=0. These are necessary restrictions on all sequences satisfying the stated hypotheses; no sufficiency or realization assertion for the indicated currents or support sets is made.
reconstruction.proof:
We first establish the uniform L¹ input for smooth normalized ω-psh functions, without assuming an additional compactness theorem. Cover X by finitely many inner coordinate balls B_i(r_i), with B_i(4r_i) in the same chart. Their intersection graph is connected. Choose A_i so that u+A_i|z|² is psh on the larger ball whenever Du≥−ω. If x is in the inner ball and u(x)≥−L, the submean inequality on B(x,2r_i), together with u≤0, bounds the integral of −u on the inner ball by a constant times L+1. Start in a ball containing a maximum point, where L=0. Each nonempty overlap with another inner ball has fixed positive volume; the integral bound supplies a point in that overlap with u bounded below. The same submean estimate then bounds the next ball. Propagating along the finite connected graph and using comparison of coordinate and metric volumes proves ∫|u|ωⁿ≤C. Hence ∫|w_j|ωⁿ=O(s_j).

Put A_j=ω+Dw_j=(1−s_j)ω+H_j. Its binomial expansion consists of positive measures. For s_j<1/2 it gives
b≥binom(n,k)(1−s_j)^(n−k)∫ω^(n−k)H_j^k,
which proves every stated mixed-mass bound, including k=0. Positive currents with bounded trace mass are weakly relatively compact: their coefficient measures have bounded variations, by positivity and polarization. A finite diagonal extraction yields simultaneous limits H_j^k→K_k.

Integration by parts and the L¹ estimate give
∫ω^(n−1)H_j=s_jV_ω+∫w_jD(ω^(n−1))=O(s_j),
so K_1=0. For any given smooth Gauduchon metric γ the same calculation is exact:
∫γ^(n−1)H_j=s_j∫γ^(n−1)ω.

The identity Dw_j=H_j−s_jω gives useful polynomial estimates. For l≤n−1 the integrals ∫ω^(n−l)(Dw_j)^l are uniformly bounded, since their expansions are signed sums of the bounded positive mixed masses. More generally, against any fixed smooth test form,
H_j^k−(Dw_j)^k→0,
with O(s_j): every term in the difference contains a factor s_j and a lower power H_j^q, q<k. Smooth-test bounds follow from the trace-mass bounds.

Since dH_j=s_jdω, d(H_j^k)=ks_jdω∧H_j^(k−1)→0. Thus every K_k is d-closed. For a smooth d-closed form η of degree 2n−2k, Stokes gives
∫η(Dw_j)^k=∫η d(d^cw_j∧(Dw_j)^(k−1))=0.
The polynomial difference estimate passes this zero pairing to K_k.

The integral of the exact top form (Dw_j)^n is zero. In the expansion of ∫H_j^n all other terms contain at least one s_j and one of the bounded integrals just described. Consequently ∫H_j^n=O(s_j). Positivity gives convergence to zero in total variation and K_n=0. Passing to the limit in A_j^n yields
σ=Σ_(k=2)^(n−1) binom(n,k)ω^(n−k)K_k.
Every summand is positive, and their combined mass is b−V_ω. In dimension three this is 3ωK_2; in dimensions at most two the sum is empty, contradicting the positive excess mass.

Finally let θ be smooth, real, semipositive and d-closed. Its complementary power θ^(n−k) is d-closed, so ∫θ^(n−k)K_k=0. This wedge is a positive measure and therefore vanishes identically. Where θ is positive definite it locally dominates cω with c>0. Its complementary power dominates c^(n−k)ω^(n−k) in these positive-current pairings. The local trace of K_k is zero there, so K_k vanishes. The representation of σ proves the support inclusion for each θ and hence simultaneously for all of them. A globally positive d-closed θ forces all defect summands to vanish. No sufficiency assertion is made.

notes.summary: Every honest shrinking defect on the standard Hopf threefold is necessarily the Haar-fiber lift Lμ of a positive measure μ on P². Thus its support is elliptic-fiber saturated and it has no point atoms. Proof: the general positive closed carrier K satisfies α∧K=0; positivity forces K to be horizontal, and closedness forces its coefficient measure to be constant along each elliptic fiber. This applies to all such sequences, not one family.
notes.detailedSummary: Let π:X→P² be the Hopf fibration, E=C/(Z+2πiZ), and h_p the probability Haar measure on π^{-1}(p). Define Lμ by ∫φ Lμ=∫_{P²}(∫_{π^{-1}(p)}φ dh_p)dμ(p). For a defect of mass m, n4 gives σ=3ωK with positive closed (2,2) carrier K whose pairings with closed forms vanish. In particular αK=0 because α is closed semipositive. In product coordinates, positivity makes every coefficient containing a fiber leg vanish, leaving only a horizontal top-base coefficient. dK=0 forces both vertical derivatives of that coefficient to vanish; Fourier modes on E then show it is a product with fiber Lebesgue measure. Thus K=π^*τ for a positive base measure τ, and σ=3βπ^*τ=L(6τ), because ∫_Eβ=2. Hence μ=π_*σ is positive of mass m and σ=Lμ. When σ is fixed, the whole quadratic-carrier current sequence converges to (1/6)π^*μ, not just its top trace. Supports are π^{-1}(supp μ); point atoms are impossible. This is a necessity theorem on the Hopf threefold, with realizability addressed separately.
notes.text:
NECESSARY FIBER STRUCTURE FOR ALL HOPF DEFECTS.

Let π:X→P² be [z]↦[z]. Let α=π^*ω_FS and ω=α+β as in the problem. The fibers are the elliptic curve E=C/(Z+2πiZ), with local holomorphic coordinate w=log z_0. The transition functions in w between base charts are translations depending holomorphically on the base; thus there is a canonical probability Haar measure h_p on every fiber π^{-1}(p).

For a positive finite measure μ on P² define its Haar lift Lμ by

  ∫_X φ d(Lμ)=∫_{P²} [∫_{π^{-1}(p)}φ dh_p] dμ(p)

for continuous φ. This is well-defined because changes of local trivialization translate the elliptic fiber and preserve Haar probability. The bracketed fiber average is continuous in p, as follows from any local trivialization and uniform continuity on the compact fiber. Thus L preserves weak convergence of finite base measures.

THEOREM. Every defect σ of an honest smooth shrinking sequence on this Hopf threefold has the form

  σ=Lμ,     μ=π_*σ≥0,     μ(P²)=b−6.

The corresponding quadratic-carrier current converges, along the sequence on which σ is the limit, to

  (dd^c w_j+s_jω)² → (1/6)π^*μ.

In particular supp σ=π^{-1}(supp μ), and σ has no point atoms.

PROOF.

1. A closed carrier annihilated by α.

Put H_j=dd^c w_j+s_jω. Note n4 gives, after extracting a subsequence, a positive d-closed (2,2)-current K=lim H_j² with

  σ=3ω∧K.

Its pairing with the smooth closed form α is zero. Since α≥0 and K≥0, this gives the measure identity

  α∧K=0.

For clarity, this also follows directly from the Hopf identities without the general pairing argument: α is closed, ∫α(Dw_j)²=0, and

  ∫αω Dw_j=∫w_j D(αω)=−∫w_j α³=0.

Hence ∫αH_j²=s_j²∫αω²→0.

2. Positivity forces K to be horizontal.

Use a product chart U×E over a base coordinate chart U⊂P², and local holomorphic coordinates x_1,x_2 on U and w on E. On relatively compact base subcharts, α dominates a positive constant times i dx_1∧dbar x_1+i dx_2∧dbar x_2.

A positive (2,2)-current in three complex dimensions has a positive Hermitian matrix of measure coefficients indexed by the three holomorphic two-forms

  dx_1∧dx_2,  dx_1∧dw,  dx_2∧dw.

One can make this statement entirely measure-theoretic: take the sum of diagonal coefficient measures as a dominating measure and use the Radon–Nikodym densities; their matrix is positive semidefinite almost everywhere. The identity αK=0 forces the two diagonal entries containing dw to vanish. Positivity then forces every cross entry involving them to vanish as well, by the elementary positive-matrix inequality |a_ij|²≤a_ii a_jj.

Therefore K has only a horizontal dx_1∧dx_2∧dbar x_1∧dbar x_2 coefficient. Its scalar coefficient is a positive distribution/measure on U×E.

3. Closedness forces Haar constancy along the fiber.

The equation dK=0 says that both real vertical distributional derivatives of this horizontal coefficient vanish. Horizontal derivatives give no condition because it already has top degree in the base directions. On E with real periods 1 and 2π, test the coefficient against a base test function times a Fourier mode exp(2πik Re w+iℓ Im w). Either vertical derivative shows that every nonconstant Fourier coefficient is zero. Density of trigonometric polynomials among continuous functions on E then shows that the coefficient is a product of a base measure with constant fiber area. This proves locally, and hence globally by compatibility of the translation transition functions, that

  K=π^*τ

for a positive top-degree base current, equivalently a positive finite measure τ on P². Here pullback by the submersion is defined locally by this horizontal product construction; no pullback through a singular map is being used.

4. Normalization and identification of σ.

In a local base chart, s=w+bar w+log(1+|x|²). With dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂ and d^c=(i/(4π))(bar∂−∂), the vertical restriction of β is

  β|_E=(1/π) d(Re w)∧d(Im w).

Since the real periods are 1 and 2π, ∫_Eβ=2. Consequently, in the notation of the lift,

  Lμ=(1/2)β∧π^*μ.

Horizontal components of β disappear in this wedge. Also α∧π^*τ=0 because the base has complex dimension two. Therefore

  σ=3ω∧K=3β∧π^*τ=L(6τ).

Set μ=6τ. Its mass is σ(X)=b−6 and its pushforward is π_*σ, because h_p is a probability measure.

Every subsequential current limit of H_j² must have this same τ=μ/6 once σ is fixed. The coefficient mass bounds from n4 give precompactness, so uniqueness of all subsequential limits proves the stated full current convergence H_j²→(1/6)π^*μ.

5. Supports and atomlessness.

The lift of a base measure is locally its product with a full-support atomless Haar probability on E. This immediately implies

  supp Lμ=π^{-1}(supp μ),    (Lμ)({x})=0 for every x∈X.

These are restrictions on every honest shrinking sequence on this Hopf threefold. They were not inferred from the total mass identity or merely from linear current convergence. The essential additional reasoning is positivity plus closedness of the nonlinear current limit. Sufficiency of the lift condition is not proved in this note; subsequent notes give actual smooth admissible realization constructions.

reconstruction.statement:
Let X=(ℂ³\{0})/⟨z↦e⁻¹z⟩, let π:X→ℙ² be the map induced by z↦[z], and equip X with the standard metric ω=α+β, where α=π*ω_FS=dd^c log|z|² and β=d log|z|²∧d^c log|z|², using dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄ and ∫_Xω³=6. The elliptic fibers E_p=π⁻¹(p) are modeled on E=ℂ/(ℤ+2πiℤ), with local fiber coordinate w=log z₀. Let h_p be probability Haar measure on E_p, defined through these local coordinates; translation transition maps make it independent of the trivialization.

For every positive finite measure μ on ℙ², define its Haar lift Lμ by
∫_Xφ d(Lμ)=∫_{ℙ²}(∫_{E_p}φ dh_p)dμ(p),  φ∈C(X).
The fiber average in this formula is continuous in p, and L preserves weak convergence of positive finite measures. With π*μ denoting the horizontal pullback current through the holomorphic submersion π,
∫_{E_p}β=2 and Lμ=(1/2)β∧π*μ.

Let b>6, and let w_j=s_j u_j be any honest smooth shrinking sequence: u_j are genuine ω-psh, sup_Xu_j=0, s_j>0, s_j→0, and ∫_X(ω+dd^c w_j)³=b. Suppose, along the sequence under consideration,
(ω+dd^c w_j)³→ω³+σ weakly.
Then there is a positive measure μ=π_*σ on ℙ² with μ(ℙ²)=b−6 such that
σ=Lμ.
For H_j=dd^c w_j+s_jω, the full current sequence along this same measure-convergent sequence satisfies
H_j²→(1/6)π*μ.
Its limit K=(1/6)π*μ is positive and d-closed, satisfies α∧K=0, and obeys σ=3ω∧K.

Consequently,
supp σ=π⁻¹(supp μ),
and σ({x})=0 for every x∈X. Thus every honest shrinking defect on this Hopf threefold has fiber-saturated support and probability Haar conditional measures on its elliptic fibers, and has no point atoms. This is a necessary-structure theorem for all such sequences; sufficiency of the lift condition is not asserted here.
reconstruction.proof:
On a projective chart write z=e^w(1,y_1,y_2). The fiber coordinate is modulo Z+2πiZ; changes of trivialization translate w by a holomorphic function of y. Thus π is locally a product with the connected elliptic curve E. Probability Haar area is independent of these translations. Here s=w+bar w+log(1+|y_1|²+|y_2|²). On a fiber β=(i/(2π))dw∧dbar w=dx∧dy/π. A fundamental rectangle has area 2π, so ∫E_pβ=2 and β|E_p=2h_p.

In the local products, integrating a continuous φ over the fiber gives a continuous base function. This proves weak continuity of L. Define the horizontal pullback current of a base measure as its distributional pullback, independent of w, in these product charts. Translation transitions make these definitions agree. Testing and integrating along the fibers yields Lμ=(1/2)β∧π*μ.

Apply n4 to the arbitrary honest sequence. Every subsequential carrier-square limit K is positive and d-closed, and satisfies σ=3ωK. Because α is globally d-closed and semipositive, n4 gives ∫αK=0. Its wedge is a positive measure, so αK=0.

We reconstruct the resulting current structure locally. A positive (2,2)-current in dimension three is represented relative to complementary two-index forms by a positive Hermitian matrix of coefficient measures. Wedging against iℓ∧bar ℓ for all covectors ℓ and polarizing establishes this representation. The form α is positive definite in the two base directions; αK=0 therefore forces the corresponding first two diagonal measures to vanish. Positivity forces their rows and columns to vanish as well. More explicitly, take Radon–Nikodym derivatives of the matrix entries with respect to the trace measure and use the positive-matrix inequality |a_ab|²≤a_aa a_bb. Thus K has only the horizontal top coefficient: it is a scalar distribution times dy_1∧dbar y_1∧dy_2∧dbar y_2, with the positive normalizing constants.

The equation dK=0 forces both real fiber derivatives of this coefficient to be zero. On U×E, test against a base test function and expand fiber tests into Fourier modes. All nonconstant modes vanish under these derivative conditions; only the Haar average remains. Consequently K=π*τ for a positive base measure τ on U. Connected fibers and the translation transitions make these local measures glue. This proves a metric-independent lemma: a positive d-closed (2,2)-current annihilated by α is a horizontal pullback.

Since α∧π*τ=0, σ=3β∧π*τ=L(6τ) and π_*σ=6τ. Therefore μ=π_*σ has mass b−6, σ=Lμ, and K=(1/6)π*μ. Every convergent carrier subsequence has this same K. Relative compactness from n4 then proves convergence of the entire carrier-square sequence along the assumed measure-convergent sequence.

If p is outside supp μ, the inverse image of a zero-measure base neighborhood has zero lift measure. Conversely any neighborhood of x over p∈supp μ contains a base neighborhood times a nonempty fiber open set in a local product. That fiber open set has positive Haar probability, so the neighborhood has positive lift mass. This proves supp Lμ=π⁻¹(supp μ). Finally the disintegration formula gives Lμ({x})=μ({π(x)})h_{π(x)}({x})=0. The argument concerns all honest sequences and asserts necessity only.

notes.summary: Constructs honest smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequences on the Hopf threefold whose entire defect is m times Haar probability on any prescribed elliptic fiber. Such a fiber is globally ω-pluripolar, so defects MAY charge pluripolar sets, even with full mass. The construction pulls the diffuse realization through degenerating linear automorphisms, repairs the curvature bound, identifies complete carrier limits, and exactly rescales mass.
notes.detailedSummary: From n2 and n5 obtain a smooth fixed-excess-mass source sequence f_k=s_k u_k whose currents H_k² converge to (m/6)α². For each fixed A∈GL(3,C), choose C_A≥1 with A^*ω≤C_Aω. Then f_k∘A has positive repaired carrier H_k^A=A^*H_k+s_k(C_Aω−A^*ω), curvature parameter t_k=C_As_k, and (H_k^A)²→(m/6)π^*(a^*ω_FS²), where a is the induced projective automorphism. Mixed repair terms have mass O_A(s_k²). The complete defect is L(m a^*ω_FS²), and its mass is m because ∫a^*ω_FS²=1. The quadratic mass identity produces a final multiplier λ_k→1 giving exact mass b and smooth normalized admissibility. For a_j induced by diag(R_j^{-1},1,1), a_j^*ω_FS²=(a_j^{-1})_*ω_FS²→δ_[1:0:0]. Choose actual sufficiently late members of the fixed-A_j constructions diagonally, retaining each prescribed ε_j and exact mass. Continuity of L proves the full local weak limit σ=m h_p. For p=[1:0:0], ψ=log((|z_1|²+|z_2|²)/|z|²) is genuine ω-psh and −∞ precisely on π^{-1}(p); unitary rotations cover every p. Thus the defect charges a globally ω-pluripolar curve with full mass.
notes.text:
THEOREM (prescribed pluripolar fiber defect).

Let m=b−6>0. For every p∈P² and every positive ε_j→0, there are smooth normalized genuine ω-psh U_j and 0<r_j<ε_j with

  M(r_jU_j)=b,
  (ω+dd^c(r_jU_j))³ → ω³+m h_p,

where h_p is the probability Haar measure on the elliptic fiber E_p=π^{-1}(p). The full excess mass m is concentrated on a globally ω-pluripolar set E_p.

PROOF.

1. Obtain a source current limit, not merely a source volume limit.

Use the honest diffuse realization from n2, with excess mass m. Denote its functions by f_k=s_k u_k and its positive carriers by H_k=dd^c f_k+s_kω. Its defect is (m/6)ω³=L(mω_FS²). Here ∫_{P²}ω_FS²=1: one can derive this normalization directly from V=6, ω³=3α²β, and ∫_Eβ=2 as computed in n5.

By the necessity/uniqueness theorem n5, the entire source carrier current sequence satisfies

  H_k² → (m/6)α².

Also H_k has mass O(s_k), by its Gauduchon trace. This stronger current statement is indispensable for the transformation argument.

2. Transform by a fixed linear automorphism and repair the lower curvature bound.

Every A∈GL(3,C) commutes with the deck dilation and defines a holomorphic automorphism of X. Let a be its projective automorphism of P². Choose a finite constant C_A≥1 such that A^*ω≤C_Aω, and put R_A=C_Aω−A^*ω≥0.

The smooth function f_k^A=f_k∘A satisfies dd^c f_k^A≥−C_As_kω. Its positive carrier for the parameter t_k=C_As_k is

  H_k^A=dd^c f_k^A+t_kω=A^*H_k+s_kR_A≥0.

For fixed A, the difference

  (H_k^A)²−A^*(H_k²)=2s_k A^*H_k∧R_A+s_k²R_A²

is positive and has current mass O_A(s_k²). The estimate uses mass(A^*H_k)=O_A(s_k), which follows by fixed-metric comparison from mass(H_k)=O(s_k). Therefore

  (H_k^A)² → (m/6)A^*α²=(m/6)π^*(a^*ω_FS²).

Multiplying by the fixed ω gives the complete carrier-measure limit

  3ω∧(H_k^A)² → (m/2)β∧π^*(a^*ω_FS²)
                   =L(m a^*ω_FS²).

It has mass m, because a is a diffeomorphism and ∫a^*ω_FS²=1.

3. Exact mass and normalized admissibility after transformation.

Let d_k^A=M(f_k^A)−6. By the exact identities in n1,

  d_k^A=3∫ω(H_k^A)²−3t_k²V →m.

In particular it is positive for all sufficiently late k. Set λ_k^A=√(m/d_k^A)→1. The mass identity gives

  M(λ_k^Af_k^A)=6+m=b

exactly. The underlying function u_k^A=(u_k∘A)/C_A is smooth, has supremum zero, and satisfies

  ω+dd^c u_k^A≥ω−C_A^(−1)A^*ω≥0.

Thus λ_k^Af_k^A=r_k^A u_k^A with r_k^A=λ_k^AC_As_k→0. Its carrier is λ_k^AH_k^A, so n1 proves the full weak measure limit

  (ω+dd^c(λ_k^Af_k^A))³ → ω³+L(m a^*ω_FS²).

All potentials here are actual smooth admissible ones. No formal pushforward assertion for nonlinear Monge–Ampère measures is used.

4. Degeneration to any prescribed fiber.

First take p_0=[1:0:0]. Let R_j→∞ and let A_j=diag(R_j^(−1),1,1), with induced projective map a_j. Since a_j is a diffeomorphism,

  a_j^*ω_FS²=(a_j^(−1))_*ω_FS².

For every q=[q_0:q_1:q_2] with q_0≠0, a_j^(−1)(q)=[R_jq_0:q_1:q_2]→p_0. The exceptional hyperplane {q_0=0} has zero smooth volume. Dominated convergence applied to each continuous test function therefore proves

  a_j^*ω_FS² → δ_{p_0}.

The fiber-average characterization in n5 shows that L is weakly continuous. Hence

  L(m a_j^*ω_FS²) → m h_{p_0}.

For each fixed A_j, step 3 supplies an entire honest sequence converging to its indicated defect. Choose one sufficiently late actual member so that its shrinking parameter is <ε_j and its Monge–Ampère measure is within 1/j of ω³+L(m a_j^*ω_FS²) on the first j functions in a fixed dense collection of continuous tests. It has exact mass b already. These deterministic diagonal choices prove

  (ω+dd^c w_j)³ → ω³+m h_{p_0}

against every continuous test. They retain smooth normalized ω-psh underlying potentials and exact parameters 0<r_j<ε_j. A fixed unitary transformation gives the same construction for any p.

The capacity and fixed-level conclusions in the problem apply because the final sequence is an honest shrinking sequence of precisely its specified class.

5. The supporting fiber is genuinely globally ω-pluripolar.

For p_0=[1:0:0], define

  ψ([z])=log((|z_1|²+|z_2|²)/|z|²).

This is well-defined under the deck action, has the canonical upper representative, is locally a genuine psh logarithm minus the smooth s, and satisfies dd^cψ≥−α. Thus ω+dd^cψ≥β≥0. Its −∞ locus is exactly E_{p_0}. It is a nontrivial genuine ω-psh function, so E_{p_0} is even globally ω-pluripolar. Rotate by a unitary map for any other p. The defect m h_p assigns mass m to this pluripolar curve.

Thus the original pluripolarity question has both kinds of realizable examples: n2 gives no pluripolar charge; this note gives full pluripolar charge. These examples remain non-atomic as point measures, in agreement with n5. The argument concerns the standard Hopf threefold, and does not claim the same prescribed fiber geometry on arbitrary Hermitian manifolds.

reconstruction.statement:
Let X=(ℂ³\{0})/⟨z↦e⁻¹z⟩ carry the standard Hopf metric ω=α+β with dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄ and ∫_Xω³=6. Let π:X→ℙ² be the elliptic fibration, E_p=π⁻¹(p), and let h_p be probability Haar measure on E_p, using its local identification with ℂ/(ℤ+2πiℤ). Put M(f)=∫_X(ω+dd^c f)³.

For every b>6, every p∈ℙ² and every sequence of positive numbers ε_j→0, there exist smooth normalized genuine ω-psh functions U_j and parameters 0<r_j<ε_j such that, writing m=b−6 and w_j=r_jU_j,
sup_XU_j=0,
ω+dd^c U_j≥0,
ω+dd^c w_j≥(1−r_j)ω≥(1−ε_j)ω,
M(w_j)=b,
and
(ω+dd^c w_j)³→ω³+m h_p weakly against every continuous function on X.
The functions w_j converge to zero in capacity. For every fixed T>0,
1_{w_j≥−T}(ω+dd^c w_j)³→ω³ in total variation,
and
1_{w_j<−T}(ω+dd^c w_j)³→m h_p weakly.
The coefficient and Gauduchon-trace convergence conclusions for honest shrinking sequences also hold.

Each E_p is globally ω-pluripolar. For p₀=[1:0:0], the canonical upper representative of
ψ([z])=log((|z₁|²+|z₂|²)/|z|²)
is a nontrivial genuine ω-psh function, satisfies dd^cψ≥−α and ω+dd^cψ≥β≥0, and has {ψ=−∞}=E_{p₀}; unitary rotations give the corresponding assertion for every p.

The realized defect σ=m h_p has σ(E_p)=m, is supported exactly on E_p, and has no point atoms. Thus all excess mass may charge a globally ω-pluripolar curve while the sequence retains the exact smooth, normalized, fixed-mass and shrinking constraints. This supplies prescribed-fiber realizations on the stated Hopf threefold, not a classification on arbitrary Hermitian manifolds.
reconstruction.proof:
Let m=b−6. By n2 choose a source f_k=s_ku_k of exact mass b with standard defect (m/6)ω³. Since L(ω_FS²)=ω³/6, n5 identifies its carrier limit as
H_k²→K=(m/6)π*ω_FS², where H_k=Df_k+s_kω.

Fix an automorphism a of X induced by an invertible linear map of C³ and put γ=a⁻¹. It descends because it commutes with scalar dilation. Choose C_a>0 with γ*ω≤C_aω. Put
F_k=f_k∘γ, t_k=C_as_k,
J_k=DF_k+t_kω=γ*H_k+s_k(C_aω−γ*ω)≥0.
For this fixed map, the square expansion and bounded trace masses show J_k²→γ*K; each error contains a factor s_k and a fixed smooth form. Let a_base be its projective automorphism. Since γ_base=a_base⁻¹, pullback of the base top measure gives
γ*K=(m/6)π*((a_base)_*ω_FS²),
3ωγ*K=L(m(a_base)_*ω_FS²).
The latter measure has mass m, using ∫E_pβ=2. By n1,
m_k:=M(F_k)−6=∫3ωJ_k²−3t_k²V→m.
Eventually m_k>0. Set λ_k=sqrt(m/m_k), w_k=λ_kF_k, r_k=λ_kt_k, U_k=F_k/t_k. Then sup U_k=0, DU_k≥−ω, w_k=r_kU_k and M(w_k)=b exactly. The carrier is λ_kJ_k and λ_k→1. The total variation estimate of n1 therefore proves the full weak measure limit
(ω+Dw_k)³→ω³+L(m(a_base)_*ω_FS²)
against every continuous test.

For p_0=[1:0:0], take a_L induced by diag(L,1,1), L→∞. Outside the hyperplane z_0=0, a_L's projective map tends pointwise to p_0. The hyperplane has zero smooth ω_FS² volume. Dominated convergence gives m(a_L_base)_*ω_FS²→mδ_p0, and weak continuity of L gives convergence of these defects to mh_p0.

Choose L_j→∞. For each fixed L_j choose a sufficiently late term from the preceding actual-potential construction with r_j<min(ε_j,1/j) and error <1/j on the first j tests of a countable uniformly dense family in C(X). This diagonal sequence has exact mass b at every index, and bounded masses extend its convergence to every continuous test. Its potentials are explicitly λ_k f_k∘a_L⁻¹, with underlying U_k=(u_k∘a_L⁻¹)/C_aL. They are smooth normalized genuine ω-psh functions and satisfy ω+Dw_j≥(1−r_j)ω≥(1−ε_j)ω. A unitary rotation provides the same construction for every prescribed p.

For pluripolarity, ψ=log(|z_1|²+|z_2|²)−log|z|² has its canonical value −∞ when the numerator is zero. The first term is genuinely psh; the second is smooth on C³\{0}. Their difference is scalar-invariant and descends to X, is nontrivial, and satisfies Dψ≥−α. Hence ω+Dψ≥β≥0. Its −∞ locus is exactly E_p0. Unitary rotations yield every fiber. Haar probability has full support on its fiber and no atoms, so mh_p is supported exactly on E_p and assigns it mass m.

Every constructed sequence is honest shrinking. The task's capacity, fixed shallow/deep and linear conclusions apply. The linear conclusions can alternatively be checked as in n2 by the positive first carrier trace and the Gauduchon integration identity. These are prescribed-fiber examples on this manifold, not a general-manifold classification.

notes.summary: On the Hopf threefold, realizable defects at a fixed mass are closed under arbitrary probability mixtures of their translates by the compact transitive ω-isometry group. Given any already realizable σ and any probability ρ on G, actual smooth honest shrinking sequences realize A_ρσ=∫g^*σ dρ. Singular or atomic ρ are handled by bounded-density approximation and diagonal parameter choices. This is a conditional orbit-convex-hull theorem, not arbitrary-measure realization or a proof of pluripolar-charging examples.
notes.detailedSummary: Use n1 to replace a source defect sequence by positive quadratic carriers ν_k→σ of mass m+o(1). Approximate an arbitrary probability ρ on G by probabilities ρ_j with densities bounded by finite C_j relative to invariant group probability. Average N_j independent translates of the same source potential with coefficient 1/√N_j. The expected off-diagonal quadratic mass is at most 3(N_j−1)C_j²s_k²V because the averaged positive (1,1)-form is ≤C_js_kω. Select a source subsequence so s_kC_j√N_j→0, and use bounded carrier masses plus elementary variance estimates to choose deterministic empirical samples. The diagonal measures converge to ∫g^*σ dρ; uniform convergence of testing ν_k against φ∘g^−1 follows from compactness of G. The exact final mass correction and nonlinear limit are as in n2. Thus finite convex combinations and arbitrary orbital mixtures are realizable with the same excess mass and any prescribed shrinking bounds. In particular θσ+(1−θ)(m/V)ω³ is realizable. If a source σ charges a pluripolar set, this mixture gives a full-support charging example, but existence of such a source is not established here.
notes.text:
THEOREM (orbital convex-hull realization on the standard Hopf threefold).

Fix m=b−V>0. Suppose σ is any defect already realized by an honest smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequence on this Hopf threefold:

  f_k=s_k u_k,  sup u_k=0,  ω+dd^c u_k≥0,  s_k→0,
  M(f_k)=V+m,
  (ω+dd^c f_k)³ → ω³+σ.

Let G=U(3)×(R/Z) be the compact transitive ω-preserving group constructed in n2. For every probability measure ρ on G, the measure

  A_ρσ:=∫_G g^*σ dρ(g)

is the defect of another honest smooth shrinking sequence of exact mass V+m. The new parameters can obey any prescribed positive bounds ε_j→0. No regularity of ρ is required.

This theorem is conditional on the source defect σ being realizable. It does not assert that every positive measure of mass m is realizable.

PROOF.

1. Positive carriers of the source sequence.

Put H_k=dd^c f_k+s_kω≥0 and ν_k=3ω∧H_k². By n1,

  ν_k → σ weakly,  ν_k(X)=m+3s_k²V,
  ∫g^*H_k dh(g)=s_kω,

where h is the invariant group probability from n2.

2. A bounded-density averaging law controls all positive mixed terms.

First let ρ_j have a density bounded by a finite number C_j relative to h. Define

  B_{k,j}=∫g^*H_k dρ_j(g).

As a positive (1,1)-form it satisfies 0≤B_{k,j}≤C_j s_kω. For independent translates g_l,g_a drawn from ρ_j,

  E[∫ω∧g_l^*H_k∧g_a^*H_k]
  =∫ω∧B_{k,j}² ≤C_j²s_k²V.

The inequality follows pointwise from positivity and B_{k,j}≤C_js_kω, either by diagonalizing relative to ω or expanding positive wedges. For

  W=N^(−1/2)∑ f_k∘g_l,
  K=dd^c W+s_k√N ω=N^(−1/2)∑g_l^*H_k,

the carrier decomposition from n2 is

  3ωK²=D+C,
  D=(1/N)∑g_l^*ν_k,
  C=(6/N)∑_{l<a}ω∧g_l^*H_k∧g_a^*H_k≥0.

Its mixed term therefore satisfies

  E[C(X)]≤3(N−1)C_j²s_k²V.

The empirical diagonal D has expected measure A_{ρ_j}ν_k. For every real test φ of sup norm ≤1 its variance is at most (m+3s_k²V)²/N, independently of the density bound C_j.

3. Arbitrary laws ρ can be approximated while keeping the mixed terms negligible.

Choose probabilities ρ_j with bounded densities relative to h and ρ_j→ρ weakly. This can be constructed without a regularity theorem: take a right-invariant metric on the compact group, let η_j be the normalized h-restriction to a sufficiently small neighborhood of the identity, and convolve ρ with η_j. Each resulting density is bounded by C_j=1/h(neighborhood), and its support displacement tends uniformly to zero, proving weak convergence. Nonempty neighborhoods have positive h-mass by invariance and a finite translate cover of the compact group.

Choose δ_j↓0 and N_j→∞ sufficiently large to control the first j test functions by the same variance/union-bound calculation as in n2. Then select a subsequence of source indices k_j increasing so fast that

  s_{k_j}√N_j<min(ε_j/4,1/j,1/4),
  3V N_j s_{k_j}²<m/2,
  3(N_j−1)C_j²s_{k_j}²V<δ_j/4.

This is possible because s_k→0. Markov and variance bounds then give a deterministic tuple of translates for which C_j(X)≤δ_j and D_j is within δ_j of its expectation on the first j continuous tests.

We check the expectation limit fully. For a fixed continuous φ, the functions φ∘g^(−1), as g ranges over compact G, form a compact family in the uniform topology. Weak convergence ν_k→σ and their uniformly bounded masses therefore give

  sup_{g∈G}|∫φ g^*ν_k−∫φ g^*σ|→0.

To prove this elementary uniform statement, use a finite uniform ε-net of the family and apply weak convergence at the finitely many net functions; the remaining error is bounded by ε times the sum of the two masses. Also g↦∫φ g^*σ is continuous. Hence ν_{k_j}→σ and ρ_j→ρ imply

  A_{ρ_j}ν_{k_j} → A_ρσ weakly.

It follows that D_j→A_ρσ weakly, C_j→0 in total variation, and

  3ω∧K_j² → A_ρσ.

Every carrier and every empirical integral above comes from the actual smooth potentials W_j.

4. Exact normalization and complete Monge–Ampère limit.

Write τ_j=s_{k_j}√N_j. As in n2,

  d_j:=M(W_j)−V
      =m+C_j(X)−3(N_j−1)s_{k_j}²V →m,

and d_j>m/2 by our parameter choice. Put λ_j=√(m/d_j)→1. Average the underlying u_{k_j}∘g_l with coefficients 1/N_j and subtract its supremum to obtain a smooth normalized ω-psh U_j. Set r_j=λ_jτ_j and w_j=r_jU_j. Then

  0<r_j<ε_j,
  M(w_j)=V+m=b,
  ω+dd^c w_j≥(1−r_j)ω,
  3ω∧(dd^c w_j+r_jω)²=λ_j²(D_j+C_j) → A_ρσ.

The total-variation reduction of n1 proves the complete local weak limit

  (ω+dd^c w_j)³ → ω³+A_ρσ.

Because U_j is smooth normalized genuine ω-psh and r_j→0, this is precisely an honest shrinking sequence and retains the supplied capacity, shallow/deep, and linear-current conclusions.

CONSEQUENCES AND LIMITATIONS.

(a) For any finite collection g_a∈G and weights θ_a≥0 summing to one, ∑θ_a g_a^*σ is realizable at the same mass. Its support is the union of the supports of the positively weighted translated measures. The theorem also includes arbitrary weak orbital mixtures, not just finite ones.

notes.text:
CLASSIFICATION AND PRESCRIBED-MEASURE REALIZATION ON THE STANDARD HOPF THREEFOLD.

Let m=b−6>0. Let π:X→P² and L be the probability Haar lift defined in n5.

THEOREM. The set of all defects of honest smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequences on this standard Hopf threefold is exactly

  { Lμ : μ is a positive finite measure on P² with μ(P²)=m }.

Every realization can be made with any prescribed positive bounds ε_j→0 on its shrinking parameters. This classifies ALL such sequences on this named geometry, not just a radial family or just the averaging examples.

Moreover:

(i) the possible supports are exactly π^{-1}(F), with F⊂P² nonempty and closed;
(ii) defects have no point atoms but may charge pluripolar sets with any prescribed fraction of their mass;
(iii) Lμ charges no pluripolar sets on X if and only if μ charges no pluripolar sets on P².

PROOF OF REALIZATION.

Necessity is n5. We prove sufficiency while retaining actual smooth potentials, exact fixed mass, genuine ω-psh admissibility, prescribed shrinking bounds, and the full weak measure limit.

First suppose μ is finitely atomic:

  μ=mΣ_{a=1}^N θ_a δ_{p_a},   θ_a≥0,  Σθ_a=1.

Note n6 gives an honest realization of m h_{p_0} for any fixed p_0. For each p_a choose a unitary transformation g_a with g_a^(−1)(p_0)=p_a. Its induced map on fibers sends Haar probability to Haar probability, because it is a translation in the fiber coordinate in local trivializations. Thus

  g_a^*(m h_{p_0})=m h_{p_a}.

The finite orbital-mixture realization theorem n3 then gives an actual smooth honest shrinking sequence with defect Σθ_a m h_{p_a}=Lμ, exact mass b, and any prescribed small parameter bounds. Its proof explicitly averages translated smooth potentials, controls the positive off-diagonal terms, and makes an exact final mass adjustment, so this step is not a formal averaging of nonlinear measures.

For an arbitrary positive μ of mass m, take finite partitions of P² of diameters tending to zero, and replace the mass of each partition element by an atom at a point in that element. This gives finitely atomic μ_j with μ_j(P²)=m and μ_j→μ weakly. For each j use the just-proved honest realization of Lμ_j. Select one sufficiently late actual member with parameter r_j<ε_j, exact mass b, and Monge–Ampère measure within 1/j of ω³+Lμ_j on the first j functions of a fixed uniformly dense collection of continuous tests.

The selected underlying U_j remain smooth normalized genuine ω-psh. The weak continuity of L, proved in n5 through continuous fiber averages, and the dense-test diagonal selection give the COMPLETE local weak limit

  (ω+dd^c(r_jU_j))³ → ω³+Lμ.

There is no loss of exact mass at the diagonal step. Also ω+dd^c(r_jU_j)≥(1−r_j)ω≥(1−ε_j)ω. This is precisely the stipulated honest shrinking construction, so its supplied capacity convergence and fixed shallow/deep restriction statements apply.

PROOF OF THE SUPPORT CLAIM.

By n5, supp Lμ=π^{-1}(supp μ), so every possible support is fiber saturated. Conversely, every nonempty closed F in the compact metric space P² is the support of a positive measure of mass m: choose a countable dense set {p_l}⊂F and positive weights with sum m, for example m2^(−l). The resulting measure has support F, and its lift is realized by the theorem. Thus the description of possible supports is exact on this Hopf threefold. In particular a measure supported on a single point of X, or on a proper non-Haar subset of a fiber, cannot occur, even though an entire pluripolar fiber can carry all defect mass.

PROOF OF THE PLURIPOLARITY EQUIVALENCE.

We use the usual local definition of pluripolarity. For measure statements one can take measurable pluripolar sets; the argument also applies to outer measure zero by using their local −∞ supersets.

If B⊂P² is pluripolar, π^{-1}(B) is pluripolar: locally pull back a nontrivial psh function with value −∞ on B through the holomorphic submersion π. It remains nontrivial because a submersion has open image. Also

  (Lμ)(π^{-1}(B))=μ(B).

Consequently if Lμ charges no pluripolar set, neither does μ.

Conversely suppose μ charges no pluripolar set on P², and let P⊂X be pluripolar. Cover X by countably many relatively compact local product charts U×D in which P is contained in the −∞ locus of a non-identically−∞ genuine psh function h(x,w). Shrinking product charts still cover X, so we can work with a fixed smaller fiber disc D' in each chart.

The function h is locally integrable and locally bounded above. For each fixed x, its restriction h(x,·) is either a nontrivial subharmonic function or identically −∞. In the former case its −∞ set has fiber area zero. Thus positive area of P on that fiber disc can occur only for base points x where h(x,·) is identically −∞ on D'.

That exceptional set of base points is pluripolar. To see this without a global projection theorem, define

  F(x)=(1/area(D'))∫_{D'}h(x,w)dA(w).

This is a psh function on the smaller base chart, possibly −∞ at some points, and it is not identically −∞. Indeed joint local integrability and Fubini give finiteness for almost every x. Upper semicontinuity follows by reverse Fatou, using a common upper bound on the relatively compact product chart; the psh submean inequalities follow by integrating the inequalities for h(·,w). Thus F is a genuine nontrivial base psh function. If h(x,·) is identically −∞ on D', then F(x)=−∞. The exceptional parameters are therefore contained in a base pluripolar set.

Outside the countable union of these exceptional base sets, every local piece of P has fiber Haar measure zero. Since μ gives that union measure zero, the defining fiber integral for Lμ and Fubini show (Lμ)(P)=0. This proves the converse and hence (iii).

EXPLICIT CHARGING FRACTIONS AND FULL-SUPPORT EXAMPLES.

For any p∈P² and θ∈[0,1], take

  μ=mθδ_p+m(1−θ)ω_FS².

The prescribed realization is

  σ=mθ h_p+(m(1−θ)/6)ω³.

The fiber E_p is globally ω-pluripolar by n6 and σ(E_p)=mθ. The remaining smooth-volume part charges no pluripolar set. Thus any desired fraction θ of the excess mass can be a pluripolar part. For 0<θ<1 these are full-support defects which nevertheless charge a pluripolar curve. At θ=0 the defect is full-support and charges no pluripolar set; at θ=1 it is entirely carried by a pluripolar fiber. All are non-atomic as point measures.

SCOPE RELATIVE TO THE ORIGINAL QUESTION.

These results settle support and prescribed-measure realization completely on the standard Hopf threefold and demonstrate, within the exact honest shrinking constraints, both non-pluripolar-charging and pluripolar-charging behaviors. They are not inferred from the supplied integrated fiber-energy identity alone. The key ingredients are the general closed-carrier restriction, its Hopf horizontal/fiber structure, an actual diffuse realization, repaired pullback through linear automorphisms, and actual potential-level mixture constructions.

For general connected compact Hermitian manifolds, n4 supplies genuine necessary current/support restrictions, and the Hopf examples disprove any universal claim that defects must avoid pluripolar sets or must charge them. A sufficiency/classification theorem for arbitrary Hermitian manifolds is not proved here. In particular the fiber-lift formula is asserted only for this Hopf geometry, not for every manifold with infinite upper bounded-potential mass.

COMPLETE HOPF CLASSIFICATION FOR AN ARBITRARY HERMITIAN METRIC.

Fix the standard scalar Hopf threefold X and its holomorphic elliptic fibration π:X→P². Now let Ω be ANY smooth Hermitian metric on X, not necessarily the standard ω=α+β. Write V_Ω=∫Ω³ and fix b>V_Ω, m=b−V_Ω.

For p∈P² define

  a_Ω(p)=∫_{E_p}Ω>0,
  h_p^Ω=Ω|_{E_p}/a_Ω(p).

The function a_Ω is smooth, strictly positive, and bounded above and below on the compact base. This follows by integrating the smooth fiber restriction in local bundle trivializations. Define the weighted lift by

  ∫φ d(L_Ωμ)=∫_{P²}[∫_{E_p}φ dh_p^Ω]dμ(p).

It is weakly continuous because its fiber averages are continuous.

THEOREM. For this arbitrary Ω, all honest shrinking defects of fixed excess mass m are exactly

  {L_Ωμ: μ≥0 on P², μ(P²)=m}.

Every such μ has an actual smooth normalized Ω-psh realization with exact mass b and any prescribed shrinking bounds ε_j→0. Thus the support and pluripolarity classification is geometric, while the conditional fiber density depends on Ω. In particular Haar conditional density is special to the standard metric, and must not be claimed for a general Ω.

1. Necessity.

Apply n4 with background Ω. In dimension three every defect is σ=3Ω∧K for a positive closed (2,2)-current K whose pairing with every closed complementary form vanishes. The globally closed semipositive α=π^*ω_FS gives αK=0. The positivity and vertical-Fourier argument of n5 does not depend on the choice of background metric: it forces

  K=π^*τ

for a positive base measure τ. Consequently

  σ=3Ω∧π^*τ,
  π_*σ=3a_Ωτ=:μ,
  σ=L_Ωμ.

The base measure μ has mass m. This also identifies K uniquely from a fixed σ, by τ=μ/(3a_Ω).

2. A suitable source carrier exists for every target μ.

Let μ≥0 have mass m, and set τ=μ/(3a_Ω), meaning multiplication by the strictly positive continuous function 1/(3a_Ω). It is a positive finite nonzero measure. Let

  m_0=6τ(P²),   μ_0=6τ.

The standard-metric classification n7 supplies smooth f_j=s_j u_j, with sup u_j=0 and ω+dd^c u_j≥0, whose standard carriers

  H_j=dd^c f_j+s_jω

satisfy H_j²→(1/6)π^*μ_0=π^*τ, by n5. Their first-power masses are O(s_j). We may select subsequences with s_j as small as needed.

3. Repair curvature for Ω.

Choose C≥1 with ω≤CΩ and let R=CΩ−ω≥0. Then

  G_j=dd^c f_j+Cs_jΩ=H_j+s_jR≥0.

With t_j=Cs_j, its first-power mass is O(s_j). Its square differs from H_j² by

  2s_jH_j∧R+s_j²R²,

a positive current of mass O(s_j²). Therefore

  G_j²→π^*τ,
  3Ω∧G_j²→3Ω∧π^*τ=L_Ωμ.

This is a tensor-current limit, hence it gives the full local measure limit after multiplication by Ω.

4. Exact mass adjustment when Ω need not satisfy dd^cΩ²=0.

Set

  L_j=3∫Ω²∧dd^c f_j,
  Q_j=3∫Ω∧(dd^c f_j)².

The integral of (dd^c f_j)³ is zero by Stokes. Thus for every real λ,

  M_Ω(λf_j):=∫(Ω+dd^c(λf_j))³=V_Ω+λL_j+λ²Q_j.

The carrier estimates identify both coefficients:

  L_j=3∫Ω²G_j−3t_jV_Ω=O(s_j),
  Q_j=3∫ΩG_j²−6t_j∫Ω²G_j+3t_j²V_Ω→m.

For sufficiently late j, Q_j>0. Let

  λ_j=(-L_j+√(L_j²+4mQ_j))/(2Q_j)>0.

This is an explicit positive root of λ_jL_j+λ_j²Q_j=m. It tends to one. Hence M_Ω(λ_jf_j)=b exactly, without incorrectly assuming a pure quadratic scaling identity for the arbitrary Ω.

Let U_j=u_j/C. It is smooth, has supremum zero, and

  Ω+dd^c U_j≥Ω−ω/C≥0.

Set r_j=λ_jCs_j and w_j=r_jU_j=λ_jf_j. By subsequence selection, 0<r_j<ε_j. The curvature bound Ω+dd^c w_j≥(1−r_j)Ω is exact. These are the required honest smooth admissible potentials.

5. The complete local weak limit.

The carrier of w_j with parameter r_j is λ_jG_j. Its square tends to π^*τ. Also ∫Ω²G_j=O(s_j), and

  ∫G_j³=t_jQ_j+t_j²L_j+t_j³V_Ω=O(s_j).

This last identity follows by expanding (dd^c f_j+t_jΩ)³ and using ∫(dd^c f_j)³=0; G_j³ is positive, so it tends to zero in total variation. Expand the actual Monge–Ampère form into positive terms:

  (Ω+dd^c w_j)³
  =(1−r_j)³Ω³+3(1−r_j)²λ_jΩ²G_j
     +3(1−r_j)λ_j²ΩG_j²+λ_j³G_j³.

The first term tends to Ω³, the second and fourth vanish in total variation, and the third tends weakly to 3Ωπ^*τ=L_Ωμ. This proves

  (Ω+dd^c w_j)³→Ω³+L_Ωμ

against every continuous test, with exact mass b at every index. Capacity convergence and the other stipulated shrinking conclusions apply because this is the same normalized genuine Ω-psh shrinking class.

6. Infinite smooth upper mass and behavior of supports/pluripolar sets.

Infinity of the smooth upper mass transfers from the standard ω to Ω independently: choose c>0 with Ω≥cω. For every smooth ω-psh u,

  Ω+dd^c(cu)=c(ω+dd^c u)+(Ω−cω)≥c(ω+dd^c u),

so M_Ω(cu)≥c³M_ω(u). Thus arbitrarily large standard smooth masses give arbitrarily large Ω-masses.

Each probability h_p^Ω has a smooth strictly positive density relative to fiber Haar. Compactness gives upper and lower bounds for the density in the bundle. Therefore L_Ωμ and the Haar lift Lμ are mutually absolutely continuous with globally bounded positive density ratios. Their supports are the same π^{-1}(supp μ), neither has point atoms, and one charges no pluripolar set precisely when the other does. By n7 this happens precisely when μ charges no pluripolar set on P². In particular arbitrary positive mixtures of a base point mass and smooth base volume realize any desired amount of pluripolar charging for Ω as well.

The theorem covers every Hermitian metric on the named Hopf manifold. It remains a geometric classification on that manifold, not a sufficiency theorem for arbitrary compact complex manifolds.
