CONSOLIDATED RESULT ADDRESSING THE EXACT DEFECT QUESTION.

The preceding notes give a complete set of rigorously proved new support/pluripolarity and prescribed-measure realization results at the scope requested in the completion criteria. They do NOT claim to have classified the defect measures on every compact Hermitian manifold. The distinction between universal restrictions and a complete named-geometry classification is essential.

A. Universal necessary restrictions forced by honest shrinking.

For any manifold and sequence in the problem, put H_j=dd^c w_j+s_jω≥0. By n4, after a common subsequence its intermediate powers have positive d-closed limits K_k, with K_1=K_n=0, and

  σ=Σ_{k=2}^{n−1}binom(n,k)ω^{n−k}∧K_k.

By n8, each K_k annihilates every global smooth dd^c-closed complementary (n−k,n−k)-form. These are restrictions on nonlinear limit currents, proved from positivity and Stokes, not conclusions from linear convergence alone. They imply concrete support restrictions. For example, in dimension three

  σ=3ω∧K_2,
  supp σ⊂{θ³=0}

for every global smooth semipositive (1,1)-form θ with dd^cθ=0. In all dimensions, a global closed semipositive (1,1)-form positive on an open set forces σ to vanish there. More generally positive dd^c-closed complementary forms eliminate their corresponding carrier summands. These necessary conditions are not asserted to be sufficient on arbitrary X.

B. Pluripolar charging is neither compulsory nor forbidden.

On the supplied infinite-upper-mass Hopf threefold, n2 constructs actual smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequences with

  σ=((b−6)/6)ω³.

This is a prescribed smooth full-support defect and gives zero mass to every pluripolar set.

By n6 there are also actual smooth fixed-mass shrinking sequences with

  σ=(b−6)h_p

for ANY prescribed elliptic fiber E_p=π^{-1}(p), where h_p is its probability Haar measure. The fiber is globally ω-pluripolar: for p=[1:0:0], the genuine ω-psh function log((|z_1|²+|z_2|²)/|z|²) is −∞ precisely on that fiber. Thus all the excess mass can charge a pluripolar set. These defects have no point atoms, showing that pluripolar charging must not be conflated with atomicity.

For θ∈[0,1], n7 realizes

  σ=θ(b−6)h_p+(1−θ)((b−6)/6)ω³.

It assigns exactly θ(b−6) to E_p. For 0<θ<1 it simultaneously has full support and positive pluripolar charge. Therefore no universal rule requiring avoidance of pluripolar sets, requiring some pluripolar charge, or requiring proper support can hold in the class posed in the question.

C. Exactly which prescribed measures are realizable on the standard Hopf threefold.

Let L be the lift from P² with probability Haar conditionals on its elliptic fibers. Notes n5–n7 prove BOTH necessity and sufficiency:

  σ is an honest shrinking defect of mass b−6
  ⇔ σ=Lμ for some μ≥0 on P² with μ(P²)=b−6.

This applies to every honest smooth shrinking sequence on this manifold, including arbitrary choices of large-mass potentials. It is not merely a formula for one radial profile. Consequently the possible supports are exactly π^{-1}(F) for nonempty closed F⊂P². Point masses on X and non-Haar conditional measures on a fiber cannot occur; arbitrary positive base measures, including singular and atomic ones, do occur. The lift charges no pluripolar set iff its base measure charges no pluripolar set.

The sufficiency proof is an actual construction: potential-level random-translate averaging with a deterministic selection yields the diffuse carrier; repaired pullback by degenerating GL(3,C) automorphisms yields a fiber carrier; positive mixed-term estimates yield finite orbital mixtures; a dense-test diagonal selection realizes arbitrary base measures. At every stage the functions are smooth genuine ω-psh after normalization, the shrinking parameter can meet any prescribed ε_j, and an exact final mass root gives integral b. The complete local weak measures are identified through positive carrier currents; no mass-only or formal nonlinear-averaging inference is used.

D. Dependence on the metric versus the complex geometry.

Note n9 gives the same classification for every Hermitian metric Ω on the same Hopf manifold, with a necessary modification: the conditional probability is Ω|_{E_p}/∫_{E_p}Ω, not necessarily Haar. All base measures of mass b−V_Ω are realizable. The exact mass adjustment here uses M_Ω(λf)=V_Ω+λL+λ²Q and its explicit positive root; one must not transfer the standard metric's pure quadratic scaling without this correction.

E. Constraint and premise accounting.

The constructions produce actual smooth normalized admissible underlying potentials and 0<s_j<ε_j, not a differently normalized class. Hence the capacity convergence, the lower bound (1−ε_j)ω, and the fixed shallow/deep conclusions stipulated in the question are retained. The full local weak measure limits are proved separately through positive expansions and current limits. The only background existence inputs are the task's supplied smooth large-mass Hopf potentials and its stated shrinking/linear trace properties. The nonlinear reduction, closedness and pairing restrictions, horizontal-fiber lemma, invariant averaging, curvature repairs, exact roots, and measure limits have explicit proofs in the support notes. No indispensable defect-identifying assertion is imported from an unchecked Hopf-profile source.

Remaining scope: a classification or general prescribed-measure sufficiency theorem on an arbitrary different compact Hermitian manifold is not established. The universal restrictions and the complete Hopf classification are deliberately kept distinct.

σ=Σ_{k=2}^{n−1}binom(n,k)ω^{n−k}∧K_k.

∫_Xη∧K_k=0.

supp σ⊂{θ³=0}
for every global smooth semipositive (1,1)-form θ with dd^cθ=0. These are necessary conditions, not a claimed sufficiency theorem for arbitrary X.

∫_Xφ d(Lμ)=∫_{ℙ²}(∫_{E_p}φ dh_p)dμ(p).
For b>6, a measure σ is an honest smooth shrinking defect of mass b−6 if and only if
σ=Lμ for a positive base measure μ with μ(ℙ²)=b−6.
This necessity applies to every such sequence, irrespective of its choice of large-mass admissible potentials. Every such μ has a realization with smooth normalized genuine ω-psh underlying functions, any prescribed bounds 0<s_j<ε_j, exact mass b at every index, and weak convergence against every continuous test function.

(m/6)ω³,
m h_p,
and θm h_p+(1−θ)(m/6)ω³,  0≤θ≤1,
are all realizable with the same exact shrinking constraints. The first has full support and gives zero mass to every pluripolar set. reconstruction.proof:
For the arbitrary Hermitian manifold and honest sequence, n4 applies to H_j=Dw_j+s_jω and supplies the simultaneous positive carrier limits, d-closedness, K_1=K_n=0 and the defect representation. Note n8 applies to these same limits and proves the zero pairings against all complementary D-closed forms and the associated local vanishing criterion. Powers of a d-closed semipositive (1,1)-form give the general support restriction. In dimension three n8 permits the weaker condition Dθ=0 and gives supp σ⊂{θ³=0}. These are necessity assertions only.

On the named standard Hopf threefold, n5 proves that every defect, regardless of its starting admissible potentials, is a Haar lift. Note n7 proves the converse for every positive base measure of the required mass, by actual smooth potentials with exact mass at every index, arbitrary prescribed shrinking bounds and convergence against all continuous tests. Those notes prove the support classification, no point atoms, Haar fiber conditionals and both measurable and outer-measure pluripolar equivalences. Since L(ω_FS²)=ω³/6, apply sufficiency respectively to mω_FS², mδ_p and mθδ_p+m(1−θ)ω_FS². This gives the three displayed defects. Note n6 supplies the explicit genuine ω-psh function with fiber −∞ locus. Smooth-volume non-charging and positivity yield exactly the stated charges and support properties. Hence pluripolar charging is neither required nor forbidden, and proper support is not required in the class of the task.

For another Hermitian metric Ω on this same Hopf manifold, n9 proves infinite upper mass as part of its actual-potential construction. It proves precisely the weighted-lift classification L_Ωμ, with normalized Ω-area fiber probabilities, necessity for arbitrary honest Ω-sequences and sufficiency for every μ of mass b−V_Ω. Its exact mass polynomial supplies the correction at each index, and its positive carrier expansion verifies the complete local weak measure limit, not merely the mass. Its support and pluripolarity conclusions are exactly those asserted here.

Every cited realization has smooth normalized genuine underlying potentials and parameters strictly below the prescribed ε_j. Thus the positive-current inequality and all capacity, fixed shallow/deep, coefficient and Gauduchon-trace conclusions given for honest shrinking sequences in the task are retained. This is a complete classification on the stated Hopf manifold, including every Hermitian metric there. For a different manifold only the necessary carrier and support restrictions have been proved, not a prescribed-measure sufficiency theorem.
